Republic of the Philippines PINOY DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II TAPæ EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY"E MAY 0 4 2011 MAYOR CELSO L. LOBREGAT City of Zamboanga DILG Opinion No. 13 S. 2011 Subject: QUERY ON THE ISSUE OF COMPENSATION IN RELATION TO THE HONORARIA RECEIVED FOR ATTENDING THE BOARD OF REGENTS-WESTERN MINDANAO STATE UNIVERSITY (BOR-WSMU) MEETINGS Dear Mayor Lobregat: This has reference to your query on the above subject arising from your designation as representative of Cong. Juan Edgardo M. Angara who sit as one of the Board of Regents of Western Mindanao State University. As correctly stated, DILG Opinion No. 6, Series Qf 2011 emphasized that you shall receive NO ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION while acting as representative of Cong. Angara in the BOR-WSMU special and regular meetings. This holds true even as of this writing for that is one of the limitations imposed upon elective officials. In your present letter, though, you mentioned that you have been receiving HONORARIA for attending the said BOR-MSWU meetings. Citing the opinion of your City Legal Officer, you further claim that the honoraria you receive is in the nature of a "reimbursement" for necessary expenses incurred for attending those meetings. Your further anchor your position by citing Section 3 of RA 8292 or the Higher Education Modernization Act of 1997 wherein reimbursement to members for necessary expenses incurred in their attendance of meetings of the Board is allowed, as well as Department of Budget and Management Circular No. 2003-06 dated 29 September 2003 wherein duly authorized representatives of ex-oficio and other members of collegial bodies and board of regents/trustees of state universities and colleges are entitled to per diems. Now the issue to be resolved by way of this opinion is whether the honorarium you receive for attending the special and regular meetings of the BOR-WMSU constitute COMPENSATION. In addressing your query, it is viewed that an honorarium and even per diem are distinct and separate from compensation, as distinguished by law and jurisprudence. HONORARIUM is a gesture of appreciation for the service of one with expertise of professional standing in recognition of his broad and superior knowledge in specific fields. It is given to officials/employees not as a matter of obligation but in appreciation for services which admit of no compensation in money. (Teodoro Santiago vs. COA, GR No. 92284, July 12, 1991, emphasis supplied).

Honorarium also comes in the form of extra monetary remuneration paid to a government official and/or employee by virtue of his office, position or in connection with the function of his office or in the discharge of his duties. (CSC Resolution No. 001523, Gloria Tabuyo, 29 June 2000, emphasis supplied). In the case of Government Service Insurance System vs Civil Service Commission, G.R. No. 98395, 28 October 1994, the Supreme Court cited COMPENSATION as one that excludes per diem, bonus, allowances, overtime pay, pay or compensation given in addition to the base pay of the position or ranks as fixed by law: "Compensation" is defined by Section I(c) of R.A. No. 1573, which amended Section I(c) Of C.A. No. 186 (Government Service Insurance Act), thus: (c) "Salary, pay, or compensation" shall be construed as to exclude all bonuses, per diems, allowances and overtime pay, or salary, pay or compensation given in addition to the base pay of the position or rank as fixed by law or regulations (Emphasis supplied). A similar definition is provided in Section 2(i) of P.D. No. 1146: (i) Compensation — the basic pay or salary received by an employee, pursuant to his employment/appointments, excluding per diems, bonuses, overtime pay, and allowances (Emphasis supplied). " Moreover, RA 8292 or the Higher Education Modernization Act of 1997 is a special law that clearly echoes the same constitutional limitation on double compensation by providing for REIMBURSEMENT of necessary expenses incurred by board members in their attendance of meetings, instead of receiving compensation therefor. DBM Circular No. 2003-06, on the other hand, provides for the payment of PER DIEM instead of compensation to board of regents/trustees attending the board meetings. Thus, the honorarium, per diem, or reimbursement do not amount to a compensation because the former items, as the law and jurisprudence have provided, are exclusions to the definition of compensation. We hope that the foregoing have sufficiently addressed your query. Warmest regards, . ROBREDO S retary Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR ANO LOCAL GOVERNMENT IN REPLYIW, pts CITE: SILG11-004372 4
